judges.19.p1.b1.text: Now in those days, when there was no king in Israel,

judges.19.p1.b2.text: A Levite who lived in the remote hill country of Ephraim took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.

judges.19.p1.b3.text: But she was unfaithful to him and left him to return to her father’s house in Bethlehem in Judah. After she had been there four months,

judges.19.p1.b4.text: Her husband got up and went after her to speak kindly to her and bring her back, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys. … when her father saw him, he gladly welcomed him.

judges.19.p2.b1.text: His father-in-law, the girl’s father, persuaded him to stay, so he remained with him three days, eating, drinking, and lodging there.

judges.19.p2.b2.text: Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread, and then you can go.

judges.19.p2.b3.text: Please agree to stay overnight and let your heart be merry.

judges.19.p2.b4.text: Look, the day is drawing to a close. Please spend the night. … Then you can get up early tomorrow for your journey home.

judges.19.p3.b1.text: But the man was unwilling to spend the night. He got up and departed, and arrived opposite Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), with his two saddled donkeys and his concubine.

judges.19.p3.b2.text: Please, let us stop at this Jebusite city and spend the night here.

judges.19.p3.b3.text: We will not turn aside to the city of foreigners, where there are no Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah.

judges.19.p3.b4.text: They stopped to go in and lodge in Gibeah. The Levite went in and sat down in the city square, but no one would take them into his home for the night.

judges.19.p4.b1.text: That evening an old man from the hill country of Ephraim, who was residing in Gibeah … came in from his work in the field.

judges.19.p4.b2.text: Where are you going, and where have you come from?

judges.19.p4.b3.text: … no one has taken me into his home, even though there is both straw and feed for our donkeys, and bread and wine … There is nothing that we, your servants, lack.

judges.19.p4.b4.text: Peace to you, … Let me supply everything you need. Only do not spend the night in the square.

judges.19.p5.b1.text: While they were enjoying themselves, suddenly the wicked men of the city surrounded the house. Pounding on the door,

judges.19.p5.b2.text: Bring out the man who came to your house, …

judges.19.p5.b3.text: No, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing! … Do not commit this outrage.

judges.19.p5.b4.text: But the men would not listen to him. So the Levite took his concubine and sent her outside to them, … and at dawn they let her go.

judges.19.p6.b1.text: Early that morning, the woman went back to the house where her master was staying, collapsed at the doorway, and lay there until it was light.

judges.19.p6.b2.text: In the morning, when her master got up and opened the doors of the house to go out on his journey,

judges.19.p6.b3.text: There was his concubine, collapsed in the doorway of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

judges.19.p7.b3.text: So the man put her on his donkey and set out for home.

judges.19.p7.b4.text: When he reached his house, … and sent her throughout the territory of Israel.

judges.19.p8.b1.text: And everyone who saw it said,

judges.19.p8.b2.text: Nothing like this has been seen or done from the day the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt until this day.

judges.19.p8.b3.text: Think it over, take counsel, and speak up!
